newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end lower, gold still pressured.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end lower, gold still pressured.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended lower Tuesday, with gold losing ground for the sixth day in a row.
"It looks like the gold market is targeting $332.00 an ounce, the level at which the Dutch sold gold a couple of years ago," Credit Suisse First Boston vice president Ian MacDonald said.
"But the momentum of the downtrend also appears to be waning," he said.
COMEX April gold ended down $1.20 an ounce at $341.90, but held above the contract low at $339.40 seen last Friday.
In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $339.80/30, compared to the London Tuesday afternoon fix at $339.40, and the New York close Monday around $340.85/35.
"Support around $340 appears to be holding, but renewed short selling could give way to longer term support at $330," CPM Group analyst Ted Kempf said.

Ongoing strength in the US dollar, some hedging by nervous producers, selling in Hong Kong despite the reopening of the tael market after the Chinese New Year holiday, and talk of bullion bank or central bank selling in Europe, all pressured gold to test its three year lows Tuesday.
COMEX March silver ended down 12.2 cents at $4.838 an ounce, but last week's lows at $4.790 have not yet been broken, traders noted. Estimated total silver volume was a high 33,000 lots.
Silver has been in a short term uptrend since mid-January, helped by investment fund buying and fundamentals which are not as bearish as they are for gold, analysts said.
But some of Tuesday's weakness resulted from long positions being rolled forward out of the March contract, traders said.
The weakness in silver resulted in the spot gold/silver ratio edging back up to 70.20, after seeing a 16 month low Monday around 68.80.
Gold remained weaker than platinum though Tuesday, with the April NYMEX platinum/COMEX gold spread jumping higher to end at $16.90 an ounce from $16.20 at Monday's close, a new four month high.
NYMEX April platinum ended down 70 cents at $358.80 an ounce.
NYMEX March palladium saw a correction after rallying to contract highs Monday, ending down $1.70 an ounce at $137.00, following seven straigh days of gains.
Earlier Tuesday in London spot palladium fixed at $135.00 an ounce, its highest level since May 8, 1996.
Delays in a contract deal between the Japanese palladium users and their Russian suppliers have led to sharp gains in palladium's price in the past six weeks, analysts said.
Russia accounts for about 66 pct of palladium supply.
